title: Architectural fingerprint reservoir for per-request kernel recall
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a lightweight per-request architectural fingerprint and a bounded reservoir of labeled fingerprints per model-variant to recall historically successful kernel families for similar requests. This reduces online probe overhead and improves tail latency by reusing high-confidence kernel decisions while still allowing controlled exploration for drifted workloads.
background: Current runtime relies on online microprobes and short-budget bandits for kernel choice. Probing adds measurable overhead for cold/bursty workloads and can increase latency tails when GPU occupancy or sequence-length distributions change rapidly. There is also a gap between per-job static heuristics and per-request dynamics (prefill vs decode, kv cache warmness). We need a compact, privacy-safe fingerprinting + recall mechanism that improves first‑request kernel choice without large storage or telemetry cost.
goal: Deploy an online, low-overhead recall layer: compute a 64-128 bit fingerprint at request admission, look up a small local reservoir keyed by (model-variant, hardware-fingerprint-bucket), and surface a ranked kernel family recommendation with confidence. Fall back to existing autotuner when confidence is low. Show measurable latency and cost improvements on mixed production traces.
success_metrics: Reduce p95 latency on mixed prefills by >=6% for model-variants in pilot
Lower median probe count (per 1k requests) by >=40% during steady state
No increase in failure rate or QoR regressions (synthetic evals) beyond 0.2%
Reservoir storage per model-variant <= 8KB on average
acceptance_criteria: Feature gate and canary rollout implemented in runtime and console controls
Bench harness (prefill+decode mixed) shows p95 improvement >=6% in 2/3 pilot topologies
Monitoring dashboards for recall hits/misses, confidence distribution, and any QoR diffs
Automated rollback trigger if p99 latency or QoR regressions exceed thresholds
technical_notes: Fingerprint features: hardware SKU (SM version), global memory bandwidth bucket, CUDA occupancy estimate, model-variant hash, short seqlen histogram bucket (prefill/avg/decode), kv-cache-warmness flag, recent token burstiness estimate
Fingerprint size target: 64 bits (production) with optional 128-bit experimental mode; use locality-preserving hashing (SimHash) to enable Hamming ball lookup

Reservoir: bounded LRU+weighted-count per (model-variant, fingerprint-bucket) stored in coordinator with size cap (default 8 entries). Entries: kernel-family-id, avg-latency, avg-cost, last-observed-timestamp, confidence-score

Recall policy: if confidence_score > 0.75 and entry.age < 24h use recommended kernel; if 0.5-0.75 use recommendation but schedule a low-cost probe in background; if <0.5 fall back to standard autotuner
Safety: all decisions logged to telemetry stream with sampling; QoR evals via prompt set are run on a background schedule for top-ranked recalls to detect quality regressions
Exploration budget: per-reservoir adaptive epsilon where epsilon decays as confidence grows; bounded to avoid destabilizing production
Privacy: fingerprints are not reversible; store only hashed bucket ids and aggregate metrics; customer data never included in fingerprint features
plan: Spike (2w): implement fingerprint proto, local reservoir data structure, microbench harness for lookups vs probe-only baseline
Implement recall lookup path in admission controller and a safe recommendation API consumed by the kernel picker (feature-gated)
Instrument telemetry: recall_hit/miss, confidence, probe_count, latency_by_bucket
Integration tests: compare canary workloads with and without recall; run QoR prompt suite on recommended kernel outputs
Canary rollout (10%): run on 3 heterogenous GPU topologies (A100-40GB, H100-80GB, RTX6000) with mixed seqlen traces
Iterate on bucketization and thresholding based on canary telemetry, then scale to 50% and full rollout
risks: Fingerprint collisions causing suboptimal kernel choices on rare topologies
Overfitting reservoir to transient bursts leading to increased tail latency when workload shifts
Telemetry sampling insufficient to detect QoR regressions quickly
Storage growth if we don't properly evict stale model-variant entries
mitigations: Use conservative default confidence thresholds and require time-decayed evidence before raising confidence
Add per-bucket eviction policy and global caps; provide automatic compaction job
Keep an aggressive QoR sampling schedule for newly populated reservoir entries
Start with narrow canary surfaces and hold aggressive rollback hooks in the console
